Men would be in units of 120 men each, called maniples. A legion would contain at least several maniples of each troop type.

The lowest rank, and the poorest were the Velites. They carried a few javelins and wore a tunic, sometimes a bear pelt for ease of identification. They would skirmish with the enemy and provide a screen for the upcoming battle. These guys were typically men just starting out on their own, think late teens to sometimes early twenties.

Next up were the Hastati. They were heavy infantry that wore some armor, carried a sword, and a shield and a basic helmet. They were wealthier than the Velites and therefore were obligated to provide better equipment. These guys would be the ones to first engage the enemy in (almost) every battle.

The third class were the Principes. These guys were the closest in the old Roman legions to what would later become the Legionary (and is what the Legionary was based off of). They were - in simplest terms - an upgraded Hastati. They had better armor, higher quality swords, shields, etc. They would charge in after the Hastati, and would often rotate with the Hastati back and forth to keep troops fresh in the heat of battle. The fourth and final line were the Triarii. These guys had the best armor and equipment, but were instead armed with spears.
